video.title: 5GHz 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 vs A20 Pro vs Dimensity 9600 Pro - Who's Actually Faster?

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Whisper small transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Geekbench 6: Snapdragon, Dimensity and A20 Pro scores spoken aloud, A20 Pro leads single core and multi-core is within touching distance -- lands on 'despite the 5GHz fastest clock speed on a mobile CPU, it's technically not the fastest'. The point is stated verbally, not only on screen.

Hook: the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 trails its competitors in ray tracing; he asked Qualcomm why, and they said Solar Bay Extreme isn't representative -- 'there's not a single game out there that replicates that on phone today'. Starting at 284.6 includes the spoken fps numbers and also works; ending at 343.1 adds his agreement that RT on phones is overkill.

also_ok.why: Why the Extreme outperforms the regular Elite with the same cores: offset package-on-package moves memory off the SoC so heat is pulled away better -- 'you've seen this before? Yes, with Apple's A20 Pro'. Opens on 'remember when I said', which restates its own setup.
Hot take that mobile games don't need this level of ray tracing; what they need is what Qualcomm bets on, Adreno Neural Fusion (super resolution, frame generation), demoed in Silver Palace.

Verdict: 5GHz is a milestone, 'does that make it the fastest CPU? Not at the moment' -- fastest single core is still Apple, then the upgrades he likes. Summary of the video; 442.8 ends on 'ray tracing can wait'.

negatives.why: Cold open: jokes about the name and teases 5GHz vs A20 Pro, but promises the benchmarks instead of giving them, then runs into the channel intro.
Architecture comparison with a subscribe-button gag, then core counts and clock speeds read off a spec sheet: numbers without a point.
Steel Nomad Lite fps numbers: a chart read aloud; the raster conclusion is a clause tacked on the end.
'By the way I completely forgot': Xiaomi and Motorola launch list and sign-off.
